title: Chest Pain Emergency Guidance
text: Chest pain with sweating, dizziness, shortness of breath, or pain radiating to the arm may indicate a cardiac emergency and requires urgent clinical assessment.

title: Respiratory Distress Guidance
text: Blue lips, low oxygen saturation, rapid breathing, confusion, and severe shortness of breath may indicate respiratory distress and require urgent escalation.

title: Routine Assessment Guidance
text: Patients who report no chest pain, no breathlessness, normal activity, and mild cough may be suitable for routine outpatient assessment if no red flags are present.

title: Oral Lesion Referral Guidance
text: Persistent mouth pain, non-healing mouth sores, white or red patches, or lumps in the mouth should be referred for oral medicine or ENT evaluation.

title: Anxiety-Related Symptoms
text: Anxiety can present with chest tightness, palpitations, tingling, and rapid breathing, but cardiac and respiratory red flags should be ruled out first.

title: Pediatric Fever Red Flags
text: Children with fever, poor feeding, lethargy, persistent crying, breathing difficulty, or blue discoloration require urgent pediatric assessment.
